messages.subject: Plotting mesh using "rgl" package
parts:
Hello INLA team!

I have been trying to plot inla.mesh object using different packages. 
Ultimately I want to use rgl package to plot stack multiple surfaces vertically.
Is there a way of exporting inla.mesh as spatial polygon?
Or alternatively, can I transform inla.mesh so that the resulting object looks like deldir object?
(Triangulation via deldir gives me a table of starting point & end point of each edge so I could use segment function to plot the triangulation result)

Thank you!

Munji

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Plotting mesh using "rgl" package
parts:
Hi,

you can use
  plot(mesh, rgl=TRUE)
to plot a mesh with rgl. See the help text for plot.inla.mesh for further options, such as the “col” and “add” arguments.

If you need more control, take a look at the plot.inla.mesh and plot.inla.trimesh code (in the mesh.R file in the code repository) to see how it uses points3d, lines3d, and triangles3d.

There is no general method that coverts inla.mesh objects to polyhedra in other formats than its own, nor as collections of polygons, partly because the sp package refuses to store polygons in 3D; they only allow 3D points in SpatialPoints objects. However, the storage format of inla.mesh is a very standard triangulation graph representation;
Points: mesh$loc, one point per row
Triangle-vertex index matrix: mesh$graph$tv, in counterclockwise order for each triangle.
The mesh$graph collection also has a few more elements for convenience.

Finn
